subject: Request: quick demo + sandbox questions
messages:
From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@parcelly.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: quick demo + sandbox questions

Hi Evelyn,

We signed up for the self-serve sandbox this morning and I wanted to see if we could get a short demo focused on inference latency and cost optimizations. We're Parcelly, a mid-market logistics platform in the US — we route last-mile deliveries for retailers. Our use case is dynamic ETA generation and automated customer notifications using short LLM prompts.

A few quick details to help you qualify before we schedule:
- Volume: ~1.2M events/month currently, expect 2–3x growth over 6 months. Typical payloads are small (prompt + context ~120 tokens).
- Concurrency: peaks at ~450 requests/minute during busy windows.
- Timeline: evaluating POC over the next 6 weeks; want a demo this week or early next.

I've attached a small export of yesterday's traffic (parcelly-traffic.csv) that shows our hourly pattern. Can you also send any pre-demo checklist so we can prep access and service accounts ahead of time?

Would like to include our CTO Sarah Miller (cc'd) on the call if possible — she may ask about data residency and encryption.

Thanks,
Alex Thompson
Head of Platform, Parcelly Inc.
Attachment: parcelly-traffic.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@parcelly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: quick demo + sandbox questions

Hi Alex — great to meet you, and thanks for the traffic export. Ben (my AE) and I can run a focused 30-minute session on inference economics + sandbox setup. Quick qualification Qs so we tailor the run-through:

1) SLA expectations for the POC: are you targeting p95 latency under 250ms for generation calls, or is throughput/cost the priority?
2) Are the prompts stateful (do you need KV cache across tokens for multi-turn dialogs) or purely single-shot per event?
3) Any regulatory constraints (PCI, HIPAA) beyond data residency/encryption we should plan for?

Proposed slots (PST):
- Wed 14 Apr, 10:00–10:30
- Thu 15 Apr, 11:00–11:30
- Fri 16 Apr, 08:30–09:00

If none of those work, feel free to pick a time on our calendar: https://calendly.com/redwood-demo/30min

I'll attach a short pre-demo checklist (redwood-pre-demo-checklist.pdf) with the service-account steps and a link to the sandbox workspace. If you can share which cloud region you're testing from (us-west/us-east/eu), we'll pick matching capacity to show realistic latency.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sales Development, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-pre-demo-checklist.pdf (PDF, 18KB)
From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@parcelly.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Miller <sarah.m@parcelly.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2027 16:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: quick demo + sandbox questions

Thanks, Evelyn — appreciate the quick follow-up. Answers inline below:

1) Priority: throughput and unit cost. p95 latency target is nice-to-have but not a hard blocker for POC. We want to understand trade-offs (batching vs latency, quantization impact).
2) Prompts are single-shot per event with a small context window (we do keep user history but not required in POC). No multi-turn KV cache for the initial scope.
3) Compliance: no PCI/HIPAA data in the payloads for now. Data residency: US-only preferred.

Slot that works for us: Thu 15 Apr, 11:00–11:30 PST. Sarah will be on the call to cover security questions.

Extra context:
- Expected steady state after POC: ~3M events/month, average 90 tokens/generation.
- We currently use AWS us-west-2 for our main services.

I've accepted the Calendly invite. Looking forward to the demo.

—Alex
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@parcelly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sarah Miller <sarah.m@parcelly.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Confirmed: Demo Thu 15 Apr 11:00 PST — sandbox + MAP

Great — confirmed for Thu 15 Apr, 11:00–11:30 PST. I've created a calendar invite and shared a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so we have clear next steps for the POC. Items in the MAP include:

- Sandbox access + service account created (Parcelly team)
- Baseline traffic run and latency/cost report (Redwood)
- Security brief: encryption at rest/in transit and KMS integration (Redwood)
- PO acceptance criteria and timeline (mutual)

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-pre-demo
HubSpot: HS-78945

Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (Excel, 12KB)

Agenda for the 30 minutes: 1) 10–12 min demo of sandbox showing batching/kernels, 2) 10 min cost/latency trade-offs and quantization recommendations, 3) 8 min next steps + MAP alignment.

If you can confirm the service-account email you want us to grant access to, we'll provision the workspace ahead of the call. Also — if there's a short example payload you want us to test live, drop it into the Drive folder and we'll include it in the baseline run.

Looking forward — talk Thursday.

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Sales Development, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.com | M: +1 (415) 555-0134
